messages:
alex_m: Heads-up / question — we're seeing a pattern where long-lived SA JWTs used by the Node streaming client cause mid-stream reauths to fail silently. Anyone seen this? Example: tokens minted with 24h ttl and then the stream tries to reauth after ~50m and gets 401s.

sam_infra: yep. We've seen that when the SDK's refresh path expects a short-lived access token with an aud matching the runtime endpoint. If aud is the project service account or a generic value, the runtime rejects the refresh. Quick check: what are you setting as audience when exchanging the SA JWT?

alex_m: using `aud: https://redwood.api/` because that's what older docs showed. switching to `https://api.redwood.ai/token` made one test pass but not consistent. stack trace is just a 401 during reauth, no helpful error.

maria_devex: two things — (1) streaming reauth path in SDK currently expects a token that can be exchanged for a short-lived bearer with the audience `https://api.redwood.ai/token` (we should probably make that configurable). (2) if you mint a very long-lived JWT and the runtime issues ephemeral tokens, you need the impersonation/audience flow to be correct. We should add a test that simulates clock drift + token refresh.

jordan_research: Concrete reccomendation: mint SA JWTs as small as possible for clients (1h or less) or use short-lived impersonated tokens. Also ensure the `sub` claim is the service account email and the `aud` matches the token-exchange endpoint. Example payload we use in infra: 

```
{
  "iss": "service-account@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "sub": "service-account@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "aud": "https://api.redwood.ai/token",
  "exp": 1672531199,
  "iat": 1672527599
}
```

sam_infra: SDK patch notes: Node client treats the incoming credential as either (A) an access token with a lifetime header, or (B) a JWT that needs token-exchange. If you pass a JWT but it lacks the correct aud, the client will try to exchange and the backend will NACK. We should improve error message. For quick local fix, run exchange explicitly before opening stream: 

```
# pseudo-command
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/token -d @jwt.pem -H "Content-Type: application/jwt" \
  | jq -r .access_token > /tmp/rw_token
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)
node my_streamer.js
```

alex_m: good idea. I can add that to our deploy script. Curious: what about Python client behavior? do they have the same expectation?

maria_devex: Python uses the same backend assumptions but its reauth code path is slightly different — it will attempt to refresh in-thread but doesn't surface the exchange error either. We're tracking making both clients log the raw exchange response.

jordan_research: Another gotcha — if you rely on impersonation across projects, make sure the `aud` includes the token-exchange URL for the target runtime region (we route by region+tenant). Mismatched aud => silent fallback to legacy auth which fails later.

alex_m: actionable list for me: (1) change mint ttl to 1h for streaming svc acct, (2) add explicit token-exchange step pre-stream in Node deploy script, (3) open PR to have SDK surface token-exchange errors. tagging infra for help with PR. :)

sam_infra: sounds good. ping me on the PR and I'll add the debug log for the exchange payload/response. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder: docs:service-accounts updated — see https://intranet.redwood.ai/docs/sa-token-exchange (edited)

maria_devex: I'll add a unit test that simulates a 401 during reauth and asserts we log exchange response. Minimal repro would help the SDK review.

alex_m: thanks all — will do a quick alpha deploy tomorrow and report back with timestamps.
